Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

    from datamodel=Web

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m

| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5") or SHA1 in~ ("1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5") or MD5 in~ ("1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5") or SHA1 in~ ("1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5") or MD5 in~ ("1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — From poisoned search results to GPU mining: A cryptojacking campaign abusing Scr Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027 T1053.005 T1053.005 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — From poisoned search results to GPU mining: A cryptojacking campaign abusing Scr
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("autorun.dll", "vcredist_x64.dll", "screenconnect.clientservice.exe", "simplerunpe.exe", "runtimehost.exe", "vlc.exe", "rumtimehost.exe", "installutil.exe", "regasm.exe", "regsvcs.exe", "msbuild.exe", "applaunch.exe", "addinprocess.exe", "aspnet_compiler.exe", "securityhealthhost.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath") or FolderPath has_any ("%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Caches\D3F4E2A1", "%AppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Start", "\AppData\Local\Temp\", "\AppData\Roaming\", "\Users\Public\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Caches\D3F4E2A1", "%AppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Start", "\AppData\Local\Temp\", "\AppData\Roaming\", "\Users\Public\") or FileName in~ ("autorun.dll", "vcredist_x64.dll", "screenconnect.clientservice.exe", "simplerunpe.exe", "runtimehost.exe", "vlc.exe", "rumtimehost.exe", "installutil.exe", "regasm.exe", "regsvcs.exe", "msbuild.exe", "applaunch.exe", "addinprocess.exe", "aspnet_compiler.exe", "securityhealthhost.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// Registry persistence locations named in the article
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any ("HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\WinSysCache")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Caches\D3F4E2A1*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*%AppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Start*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\AppData\Local\Temp\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\AppData\Roaming\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Users\Public\*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("autorun.dll","vcredist_x64.dll","screenconnect.clientservice.exe","simplerunpe.exe","runtimehost.exe","vlc.exe","rumtimehost.exe","installutil.exe","regasm.exe","regsvcs.exe","msbuild.exe","applaunch.exe","addinprocess.exe","aspnet_compiler.exe","securityhealthhost.exe"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
| append [
  | tstats summariesonly=false count
      from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
      where Registry.action IN ("created","modified")
        AND (Registry.registry_path="*HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WinSysCache*")
      by Registry.dest, Registry.process_name, Registry.registry_path,
         Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.registry_value_data
  | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
]
Critical

[LLM] XWiki unauthenticated XAR import via REST POST /rest/wikis/{wikiName} (CVE-2026-33137) Exploitation High
Hunts successful, unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to the XWiki REST XAR-import endpoint (/xwiki/rest/wikis/{wikiName}[/]) that return 2xx, which is exactly the exploitation primitive in CVE-2026-33137 — the import runs with no auth/authz check, letting an attacker create or update wiki documents. The Authorization-header-absent + 2xx-status combination separates exploitation from legitimate authenticated XAR imports performed by admins/migration tooling. Rationale: Built directly on the advisory's exact exploitation primitive — POST to /wikis/{wikiName} performing a XAR import with no auth check. Confirmed via XWiki docs/dev list that the real path is /xwiki/rest/wikis/{wikiName} (POST, optional ?backup=&history= params, XAR in body), so the regex on /rest/wikis/<single-segment> plus 2xx plus absent Authorization header is high-fidelity for unauthenticated exploitation vs legitimate authenticated imports. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qrvh-r3f2-9h4r • https://jira.xwiki.org/browse/XWIKI-23953 • https://www.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Documentation/UserGuide/Features/XWikiRESTfulAPI • https://devs.xwiki.narkive.com/KEuNSQkQ/xwiki-vote-add-rest-api-to-import-a-xar-file
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/rest/wikis/[^/?#]+/?($|\?)"   // /xwiki/rest/wikis/{wikiName}[/] XAR-import endpoint
| where tostring(HttpStatusCode) in ("200","202")            // import accepted/succeeded
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)              // CVE-2026-33137: import runs with NO auth header
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DvcHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpRequestBodyBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm C2/exfil egress (masscan.cloud, git-tanstack.com, getsession.org) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts outbound DNS/network connections to the Mini Shai-Hulud (TeamPCP) worm's confirmed exfiltration infrastructure used after a poisoned npm/PyPI package executes its install-time payload. These domains are credential dead-drops, not legitimate developer endpoints, so any resolution is high-fidelity. Rationale: Uses the article's extracted domains (api.masscan.cloud, git-tanstack.com, filev2/seed1.getsession.org) plus the corroborated zero.masscan.cloud:443/v1/telemetry exfil endpoint. StepSecurity/Wiz/OX/Splunk all confirm these as TeamPCP/Mini Shai-Hulud C2-dead-drop infra; VPC flow lacks domain names so cloudwatch is empty. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://www.ox.security/blog/lightning-python-package-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/npm-supply-chain-attack-detection-analysis.html

[LLM] Package-manager process harvesting cloud metadata / Vault (IMDS 169.254.169.254, ECS 169.254.170.2, Vault :8200) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts node/npm/npx/bun/yarn/pnpm or python reaching the AWS/ECS instance-metadata endpoints or a local HashiCorp Vault listener — the credential-harvesting step the Mini Shai-Hulud payload performs at install time. Package managers contacting link-local metadata IPs during dependency install is anomalous. Rationale: Anchored on the corroborated network targets the StepSecurity write-up lists (169.254.169.254 IMDS, 169.254.170.2 ECS/Fargate creds, 127.0.0.1:8200 Vault) scoped to JS/Python package-manager parents, which is the worm's credential-access step. Sentinel ASIM network has no process field so this is best-effort and noisier there. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://snyk.io/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised/

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud 'gh-token-monitor' persistence daemon (LaunchAgent / systemd) Installation High

[LLM] npm/bun process writing GitHub Actions workflow files (worm secret-exfil injection) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts a JS package-manager process (node/npm/npx/bun/yarn/pnpm) creating or modifying files under .github/workflows — the Mini Shai-Hulud worm injects a malicious workflow that serializes repo secrets via toJSON(secrets) and posts them to api.masscan.cloud, enabling self-propagation through CI. Rationale: Targets the corroborated propagation mechanism (injected GitHub Actions workflow serializing toJSON(secrets) to api.masscan.cloud) by flagging package-manager processes writing workflow YAML — file content isn't in EDR file telemetry, so the parent-process + path combo is the pivot. Endpoint-only; cloudwatch empty. Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

falsepositives:

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] BTMOB Android RAT APK SHA256 sighting in file or email telemetry · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] BTMOB C2/phishing domain contact — arbsniper.com · [LLM] Egress to BTMOB hosted C2 cluster (LATAM/Hetzner IPs, Google CDN excluded) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] BTMOB C2/phishing domain contact — arbsniper.com Command & Control High
Detects any corporate-managed device (or perimeter proxy) resolving or connecting to arbsniper.com, the only non-CDN domain ESET ties to BTMOB Android RAT infrastructure. Catches infected BYOD on corporate WiFi, Windows endpoints that fetched the phishing lure, and proxy egress. Rationale: arbsniper.com is the single non-CDN C2/phishing domain ESET attributes to BTMOB and is also cited in Cyble's Feb 2025 write-up (https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/) and Malpedia (https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/apk.btmob). Two-source corroboration — high fidelity. The other ESET IPs include Google CDN ranges (74.125.x.x, 142.251.x.x, 173.194.x.x, 192.178.x.x) which would FP catastrophically; this UC pivots on the high-signal domain instead. Cross-checked against: • https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/ • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/apk.btmob • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/btmob-android-rat-maas-builder/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001

  | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceVendor, Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName), Result=DeviceAction),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where DnsQuery has BadDomain
  | project TimeGenerated, Source=EventProduct, Host=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, Result=DnsResponseCodeName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] BTMOB Android RAT APK SHA256 sighting in file or email telemetry Delivery High
Hash-IOC sweep for the BTMOB v2.5+ APK sample corpus published by ESET (cross-referenced with Cyble). Hits if any of the 36 SHA256s land on a managed endpoint via download, MDM sync staging directory, or arrive as an email attachment — covers the delivery stage for organisations with BYOD that touches corporate mail/file infra. Rationale: 36 SHA256 hashes published by ESET, with the family corroborated by Cyble (https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/), Malpedia (apk.btmob entry), and Infosecurity Magazine. Hash-IOC matches are unambiguous when they hit — main delivery vectors for corporate exposure are (a) APKs reaching mail attachments destined for company-issued Android devices, and (b) APKs landing in a Windows download folder before sideload to a paired Android device. Includes ImFileEvent for Sentinel cross-vendor portability. Cross-checked against: • https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/ • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/apk.btmob • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/btmob-android-rat-maas-builder/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/btmob-android-rat-poses-significant-threat-with-easy-to-use-builder
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.002 T1474.003

[LLM] Egress to BTMOB hosted C2 cluster (LATAM/Hetzner IPs, Google CDN excluded) Command & Control Medium
Hunts corporate-network egress to the BTMOB C2 hosting footprint published by ESET, scoped to the non-CDN subset (Hetzner 178.156.x, LATAM bulletproof 191.96.x / 191.101.x / 200.9.x / 78.135.x / 79.133.x, Cloudflare front 104.21.64.137, 195.160.221.203). The Google IPs in ESET's IOC list are intentionally excluded because they are Google CDN ranges that would FP on every browser session. Rationale: Excludes the Google CDN ranges (74.125.x, 142.251.x, 173.194.x, 192.178.x) from ESET's IOC list which would generate overwhelming FPs on every browser session — these are Google services arbsniper.com / BTMOB happens to use for tracking/analytics, not C2. Focuses on the genuine BTMOB hosting footprint: Hetzner (178.156.x), LATAM bulletproof clusters (191.96.x, 191.101.x, 200.9.x), and the Cloudflare front (104.21.64.137). Hunting tier because the LATAM hosts may serve other tenants. Cyble's Feb 2025 write-up corroborates the LATAM C2 pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/ • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/apk.btmob

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high

// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48172")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48172")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Laravel-Lang supply chain C2/exfil to flipboxstudio.info Command & Control High
Hunts DNS lookups, SNI, or HTTP host headers to flipboxstudio[.]info — the C2/exfil domain used by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer package compromise. The domain hosts both /payload (second-stage) and /exfil (stolen secrets), so any traffic to it from a Laravel-running host or CI runner indicates active compromise. Rationale: flipboxstudio[.]info is the single attacker-controlled C2/exfil endpoint named in the Snyk advisory and corroborated by StepSecurity, The Hacker News, Socket and Cyberpress. The domain has no legitimate use, so any successful resolution or connection is high-fidelity. Hits both DNS and HTTP/SNI telemetry to catch the resolution even if the payload connection is blocked. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/laravel-lang-php-packages-compromised.html • https://socket.dev/blog/laravel-lang-compromise • https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1195.002
Data sourcesWeb Network_Resolution Network_Traffic

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info" or RemoteUrl endswith "flipboxstudio.info"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc

  | where DnsQuery has "flipboxstudio.info"
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Computer=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, ResultCode=DnsResponseCodeName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Laravel-Lang stealer file drop in .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Hunts file creation under any .laravel_locale subdirectory of a temp path. The Snyk advisory documents three artifacts under <tmp>/.laravel_locale/: an md5-hashed infection marker, a 12-hex-char .php second-stage stealer, and (on Windows) an 8-hex-char .vbs launcher. The directory name is unique to this campaign and has no benign use. Rationale: The Snyk IOC table explicitly names <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<md5>, <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<12 hex>.php, and <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 hex>.vbs as stealer artifacts; StepSecurity corroborates the /tmp staging behaviour. The directory string is unique to this campaign and matches regardless of whether tmp resolves to /tmp, $TMPDIR, or %TEMP%. The filename regex extensions tag which stage fired for fast triage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/laravel-lang-compromise
ATT&CKT1059 T1105 T1195.002

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has ".laravel_locale"
| extend Marker = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32}$", "infection_marker", "")
| extend Stage2 = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{12}\.php$", "stealer_php", "")
| extend VbsLauncher = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{8}\.vbs$", "vbs_launcher", "")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, Marker, Stage2, VbsLauncher, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".laravel_locale"
| extend Marker = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32}$", "infection_marker", "")
| extend Stage2 = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{12}\.php$", "stealer_php", "")
| extend VbsLauncher = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{8}\.vbs$", "vbs_launcher", "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, Marker, Stage2, VbsLauncher
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DebugChromium.exe execution (Laravel-Lang stealer Windows artifact) Installation High
Hunts execution of DebugChromium.exe anywhere on disk. The Snyk advisory names this binary as a Windows artifact observed on hosts infected by the Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain stealer. The name impersonates a Chrome debug build to blend in with developer tooling; there is no legitimate Microsoft/Google binary by this name. Rationale: DebugChromium.exe is called out by name in the Snyk IOC table as a Windows artifact observed on infected hosts. The string is unique - no legitimate Microsoft or Google product ships a binary by this name - so a process-create on this filename is essentially confirmation of infection. Captures parent (likely cscript.exe from UC4) for chain reconstruction. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/ • https://securityonline.info/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack-rce-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1204.002 T1195.002

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] cscript/wscript executing a script from .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Hunts cscript.exe or wscript.exe invocations whose command line references a .laravel_locale path. The Snyk advisory describes the Windows execution chain as the malicious PHP helper writing an 8-hex-char .vbs into %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\ and launching it via cscript — pairing the canonical script interpreter with the stealer's unique staging directory yields a tight signal. Rationale: Snyk explicitly documents the Windows execution chain as a .vbs launcher under %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\. The compound (cscript|wscript) + .laravel_locale leaves no realistic benign matches — neither Windows nor any common dev tool stages scripts in a directory of that name. Captures parent process so triage shows the PHP runtime (php.exe / php-cgi) that originated the launch. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1218 T1195.002

DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("cscript.exe","wscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Compromised laravel-lang Composer package: helpers.php in vendor tree Delivery High
Hunts the file write or presence of src/helpers.php under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,http-statuses,attributes,actions}/. A legitimate localization package has no reason to ship an autoload-files helper, so any host whose Composer cache contains this file pulled a poisoned tag during the May 22-23 2026 incident and should be treated as compromised until the package is rolled back and credentials rotated. Rationale: The Snyk detection guidance explicitly tells defenders to inspect vendor/laravel-lang/*/ for the presence of src/helpers.php — legitimate releases of these four localization packages do not ship a helpers file or use autoload.files. The package-name regex narrows to the four named-compromised packages (lang, http-statuses, attributes, actions) per the affected-versions table, avoiding stray matches on other laravel-lang/* repos. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277 • https://gbhackers.com/compromise-laravel-lang-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "vendor\\laravel-lang\\" or FolderPath has "vendor/laravel-lang/"
| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, FolderPath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, Package, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "vendor/laravel-lang/" or TargetFilePath has @"vendor\laravel-lang\"
| where TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Package, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Laravel Lang Supply Chain Advisory Exploitation High

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Laravel Lang Supply Chain Advisory
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("debugchromium.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages with Credential Stealer
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory · [LLM] Stealer or VBS launcher dropped into .laravel_locale temp directory · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
[LLM] C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper Command & Control High
Detects any HTTP/DNS contact with the hard-coded C2 domain flipboxstudio.info (decoded from integer array in the malicious src/helpers.php). Both the /payload fetch (stage-2 stealer download) and /exfil (AES-256 encrypted credential exfil) hit the same FQDN, so any resolution or connection is unambiguously malicious. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named C2 domain flipboxstudio.info plus the /payload and /exfil URL paths quoted verbatim. Corroborated by https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities and https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/. [LLM] cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Detects the Windows arm of the Laravel-Lang dropper: the malicious src/helpers.php writes an 8-hex-character .vbs launcher into <temp>\.laravel_locale\ and executes it silently via cscript. Process tree is php/php-fpm/php-cgi (or anything that triggered composer autoload) → cscript.exe with a .vbs path containing `.laravel_locale`. Rationale: Anchored on two article-quoted strings together: `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 random hex chars>.vbs` and the explicit `runs the payload silently via cscript` Windows-launcher behaviour. The 8-hex regex makes this near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 14d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cscript.exe" or FileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has @".laravel_locale"
   and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe"
  | where CommandLine has ".laravel_locale" and CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
     and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package Delivery Medium
Detects composer (or any file mover) writing a src/helpers.php file under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,attributes,http-statuses}/ — the article confirms this file does not exist in the legitimate packages and was injected by the attacker via fork-tag commits. Catches the supply-chain payload at composer-install time, before the dropper detonates. Rationale: Anchored on the article-quoted file name (`src/helpers.php`) plus the three affected package names verbatim (`laravel-lang/lang`, `laravel-lang/attributes`, `laravel-lang/http-statuses`). The file is novel to the malicious tags, so any write is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/fake-laravel-packages-on-packagist.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let LookbackDays = 30d;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\\\/]vendor[\\\\/]laravel-lang[\\\\/](lang|attributes|http-statuses)[\\\\/]src[\\\\/]?$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)[\\\\/]vendor[\\\\/]laravel-lang[\\\\/](lang|attributes|http-statuses)[\\\\/]src[\\\\/]helpers\.php$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
